correctness.rationale: The constant-free power-semiring instance meets f nonidentity and |f(S)|≥2. A long product in P(S) yields f of its first argument when all variables in its content are nonempty, and empty otherwise. Thus rank r has r singletons and r·2^(r−1) canonical long terms. Two nonempty sums are equal exactly when they absorb the same canonical terms, since equality is mutual absorption of their summands. The cited joins are correct: an identity holds in a join iff it holds in each generator; on F_U(r) the meet of the two subvarieties corresponds to the join of their fully invariant congruences. Taking connected components of the union therefore counts the U_delta classes. Independent finite generation/evaluation reproduces the full vectors at r=1,2,3, including rank three (1727,1065,583,511,239,188,63); their distinctness and the lower-rank collisions verify the minimum rank. There are five proper intermediates (A=U_sigma is the lower endpoint). The frozen notes overstate the script assertions: absorption_census.py checks internal agreement and endpoints rather than asserting all seven rank-three entries against constants; direct_census.py asserts the rank-three vector. Frozen code was inspected, not executed.

originality.rationale: The five intermediate integers were not found explicitly printed in the earlier paper. They are nonetheless direct mechanical instantiations of its exact necessary-and-sufficient classification of all term classes of precisely these varieties, with no new reduction or counting theorem: form the 15 normal words, take their 32767 nonempty subsets, and count distinct 15-bit signatures supplied entrywise by (3.2) and (4.4). Rank three is already the natural free generation rank in the same paper; the endpoint numbers and lower-rank collisions are already covered. This verdict is about mechanical implication, not a claim to have found the identical printed table in an older source.
residual_risks: An explicit earlier intermediate table may also exist; absence in the identified passages is not an exhaustive historical search. The demonstrated mechanical implication does not depend on finding such a table.
